1.title: Math Is Mine
1.mission: Start the year as a doer of math: tell your math story, revisit fractions, decimals, volume, and patterns, and build the habits this course runs on.
1.finalChallenge: Share your math story and show one grade-5 idea you can already explain to someone else.

2.title: Data Detectives
2.mission: Collect, display, and summarize data with center, spread, and shape to answer statistical questions — and divide multi-digit numbers and decimals fluently along the way.
2.finalChallenge: Investigate a real question with your own data set and defend the measure of center you chose.

3.title: Ratio City
3.mission: Use ratio language, tables, and equivalent ratios to compare quantities, reason about unit rates, and convert measurements.
3.finalChallenge: Design and justify a best-value mixture, recipe, or menu using ratios.

4.title: Percent Studio
4.mission: Understand percent as a rate per hundred, move between fractions, decimals, and percents, and find the part, the percent, or the whole.
skills: estimate the percent of a number
find the whole from a part
4.finalChallenge: Compare real prices and discounts and prove which offer is actually the better deal.

5.title: Area & Volume Architects
5.mission: Find area by composing and decomposing shapes, then extend the same reasoning to volume and surface area with nets.
5.finalChallenge: Design a space or container to a brief and justify every area and volume you claim.

6.title: Expression Engine
6.mission: Divide fractions, take apart numbers with factors and multiples, and write, evaluate, and prove equivalent expressions.
6.finalChallenge: Model a real plan with an expression and show a second expression that must give the same result.

7.title: Integer Outpost
7.mission: Reason about positive and negative numbers, absolute value, and position on the coordinate plane in all four quadrants.
7.finalChallenge: Map a route or location problem in all four quadrants and justify each distance.

8.title: Equation Quest
8.mission: Understand what a solution is, then write, solve, and graph one-step equations and inequalities.
8.finalChallenge: Turn a real constraint into an equation or inequality and defend the solution set.

9.title: Relationship Lab
9.mission: Connect two changing quantities across tables, graphs, and equations, and use independent and dependent variables to describe how they move together.
9.finalChallenge: Model a real situation with a table, a graph, and an equation, and show they tell the same story.

10.title: Math Is Everywhere
10.mission: Close the year by finding mathematics in art, play, invention, and the world around you — and by naming how you have grown as a mathematician.
10.finalChallenge: Show where you found math outside class this year and explain what it made you notice.
